speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) strives to provide every Singaporean with opportunities to achieve their fullest potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will ensure education remains an effective social leveller, by giving every child access to quality education, and multiple pathways throughout life to pursue their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Education remains the best way for us to sustain and strengthen social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With COVID-19's disproportionate impact on the disadvantaged, we are redoubling our efforts to make sure no child is left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will give every child a good start in life, regardless of their backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also deepen support for students with special needs – by strengthening educators' professional competencies in both mainstream and Special Education (SPED) schools, as well as opening new SPED schools and upgrading current ones.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT), we will deepen school-community partnerships to support vulnerable students and engage their families.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More Singaporeans will be able to benefit from the recently-enhanced MOE Financial Assistance Scheme and Government bursaries for students in Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will continue to support all students holistically.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We strive to foster the joy of learning in our students, so that Singaporeans are equipped not just with knowledge and skills, but also with the spark to pursue their passion and fulfil their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To achieve this, we will strengthen our team of Teachers, Allied Educators, and Education and Career Guidance Counsellors, and extend more resources for students with greater needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will create fresh opportunities for students of different backgrounds to interact and build bonds with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Students from different schools will also come together for inter-school activities like combined team co-curricular activities, the MOE-Outward Bound Singapore Challenge Programme, and Values-in-Action programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Disruptions due to COVID-19 have opened up new opportunities to reimagine teaching and learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key part of education has always been to inculcate social responsibility and resilience in our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A refreshed Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum will be progressively rolled out in all schools, to give added focus to mental health and cyber wellness education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In secondary schools, teachers will engage students in regular discussions on contemporary issues and equip them with critical thinking skills to navigate such issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To prepare students for the future workplace, our IHLs will expand efforts in inter-disciplinary learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Students can look forward to more broad-based common core curricula and access to electives, as well as new industry-relevant degree programmes that integrate knowledge from different disciplines.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also aim to give students more room to decide on their academic specialisations by introducing more common entry programmes in the Polytechnics and giving University students more time to declare their major.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through multiple pathways in our education system, we will cater to the diverse strengths and aptitudes of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to embrace a wider spectrum of skills and talents, and not just focus narrowly on academic achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From 2021, the Primary School Leaving Examination will have wider scoring bands to reduce the overly fine differentiation of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will offer students more opportunities to pursue subjects at a level suited to their strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also expand our post-secondary progression pathways for students with different aptitudes and skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By 2030, all Institute of Technical Education (ITE) graduates will have a range of opportunities to upgrade beyond a Nitec over the course of their careers, according to their interests and learning needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To cater to their different interests and learning needs, we will continue to increase the number of places in ITE's Work-Study Diplomas and full-time Higher Nitec programmes, as well as the number of places for working adults in full-time Polytechnic diploma programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also further expand the adoption of Aptitude-Based Admissions across our six Autonomous Universities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of SkillsFuture, our immediate priority is to support the efforts of the National Jobs Council in creating jobs, traineeships, and training opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our IHLs will continue to ramp up their capacity for continuing education and training, and in particular, increase their range of industry-relevant modular courses to support lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also grow SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes into a mainstream pathway by 2025 so that more students can benefit from learning opportunities both in the workplace and the classroom.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For mid-career workers in their 40s and 50s, we will provide them with additional help to refresh their skillsets, so that they can seize new job opportunities amidst economic restructuring.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our educators too must embrace this mindset of continuous learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will support them in their professional development through SkillsFuture for Educators (SFEd).
